review_candidates.title: UNFPA Egypt CO - National Consultancy for the preparation to conduct the 2028 Population and Housing Census
review_candidates.description: Hiring Office JOB DESCRIPTION Egypt Country Office/UNFPA Purpose Of Consultancy The Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) of Egypt is preparing to conduct the 2028 Population and Housing Census using a Combined Census Methodology (Base Register + Full Field Enumeration). This approach aligns with UN Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses (Revision 4). This approach combines administrative register data with field enumeration and can leverage both registers and field operations as it provides the opportunity to assess the accuracy and completeness of the available administrative data sources. In this design, administrative registers provide the population baseline and select core topics, while full field enumeration verifies data on the doorstep and collects characteristics unavailable in registers. Also, it will serve as a foundational milestone toward a fully register-based census model in future rounds. The overall purpose of this assignment is to strengthen CAPMAS’s institutional and technical capacity to assess, clean, link, and utilize administrative registers for the 2028 Combined Census and the subsequent transition to register-based statistics. This technical assistance aims to establish the statistical infrastructure within CAPMAS required to transform raw administrative files into high-quality statistical records, build an integrated secondary Statistical Population Register (SPR), and implement microdata confidentiality safeguards. Scope of work: (Description of services, activities, or outputs) Transitioning to a register-based census is especially challenging for populous countries like Egypt due to the volume of data that must be integrated. Additionally, some administrative registers are often decentralized across regional and local levels rather than centralized nationally, significantly increasing the number of data sources to process and further complicating the transition. As part of census modernization, and as a strategic secondary consideration, integration of Mobile Phone Data for Population Statistics is another important consideration. Mobile phone data—specifically anonymized and aggregated Call Detail Records (CDRs) and positioning data—offers a high-coverage source for producing frequent, timely, and dynamic population statistics. Within the scope of this consultancy, mobile phone data will be evaluated at a conceptual and methodology-design level as a supplementary "signs of life" tool to validate register population counts, while primary execution remains focused on administrative registers. While CAPMAS holds deep and long-standing expertise in traditional census operations and information management, a register-based statistical system requires additional statistical expertise, particularly in the linkage and matching of data in registers, record linkage, quality assessment and statistical control. To ensure international compliance and rigorous standards, this technical assistance is grounded in the United Nations Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses (Revision 4), the UNSD Handbook on Register-Based Population and Housing Censuses, and the UNECE Guidelines for Assessing the Quality of Administrative Sources for Use in Censuses. The administrative records in Egypt are primarily managed by various ministries and register-holders, CAPMAS will build an internal, secondary Statistical Population Register (SPR). This consultancy will enable CAPMAS technical teams to assess register readiness, execute administrative-to-statistical data transformations, build an integrated SPR backbone, and implement statistical data protection. Objectives of the Assignment Preconditions Assessment: Evaluate and benchmark Egypt’s register ecosystem against international preconditions for register-based and hybrid transitions, highlighting legal, technical, and institutional gaps. Multi-Stage Data Quality Assessment: Train and enable CAPMAS to identify and evaluate administrative data sources across Source, Input, Process, and Output quality stages. Data Transformation and Matching: Establish specialized capacity in deterministic and probabilistic record linkage, de-duplication, conflict resolution, and "Signs of Life" (SOL) activity filtering. SPR Structural Construction: Formulate the architectural blueprint and operational workflow to link individuals, addresses, and enterprises into an integrated secondary Statistical Population Register. Data Governance & Safeguards: Establish statistical disclosure control, microdata security, and inter-institutional governance frameworks. Comprehensive Scope of Work & Technical Modules Module 1: Readiness and Preconditions for Register Transitions This module establishes the foundational non-technical and institutional parameters required to secure a reliable, continuous, and lawful supply of administrative data. Legal Framework & Political Support: Review CAPMAS's legal authority under Law No. 35 of 1960 and relevant modern statistics acts to receive, process, merge, and store microdata from administrative owners strictly for statistical purposes, ensuring confidentiality. Also, a strong political commitment and formalized collaboration between administrative authorities and the national statistical office are essential for a successful transition to register-based statistics. Administrative Routines Assessment: Assess the current data collection routines, capacities and quality guidelines of partner agencies to ensure a continuous and dependable supply of high-quality data. Unified Identifier Evaluation: Assess the penetration, stability, and error rates of the 14-digit National ID across external registers. Inter-Institutional Frameworks: Draft templates for Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), data sharing protocols, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), and Service Level Agreements (SLAs) between the holders of administrative registers (Administrative Control, MoHP, MoSS, etc) and CAPMAS defining transmission frequencies, format standards, metadata sharing, and dispute resolution. Public Trust and Data Ethics: Establish transparency frameworks, data ethics assessments, and public communications regarding data anonymization and confidentiality. Other Relevant Points To Be Considered Data provision: Where appropriate, and with necessary safeguards in place, explore opportunities for collaboration with the private sector to access data that can support census operations. This might involve accessing through data-sharing agreements, private sector data such as mobile location data or utility usage records, which can be valuable for understanding population mobility or identifying signs of life. Resolving Data Overlaps and Conflicts: A combined census often draws on multiple data sources that may contain overlapping or conflicting variables. In such cases, decision-makers must evaluate and select the most appropriate source to use. Furthermore, register-based data and field data frequently yield inconsistent results, even for identical topics. To ensure coherence, weighting techniques can be applied to align the datasets, while field data can serve as a benchmark to evaluate the accuracy and coverage of register counts. Module 2: The Four-Stage Register Quality Evaluation Framework Capacity Building Must Follow The UNECE/UNSD Four-stage Quality Evaluation Framework To Systematically Assess Quality Across The Entire Data Journey. CAPMAS And The Expert Will Consider Splitting The Training Into Two Phases, One On Assessing The Registers And Two On Developing The Statistical Population Register Source-Level Quality: Evaluating legal basis, register keeper trust, metadata completeness, and data transfer logistics. Input-Level Quality: Assessing raw microdata completeness, representation errors (under-coverage and over-coverage), measurement errors, and timestamp alignment. Process-Level Quality: Measuring linkage accuracy (false positives vs. false negatives), imputation rates, and edit failure rates. Output-Level Quality: Validating accuracy, relevance, coherence, and comparability with past census benchmarks. Module 3: Administrative-to-Statistical Transformation & Linkage This module covers the core statistical algorithms and processing rules required to integrate disparate databases into a single coherent census database. Concept and Classification Harmonization: Mapping administrative concepts (e.g., registered address, formal employment) to UN census definitions (e.g., usual residence, labor force status). Deterministic and Probabilistic Record Linkage: Training on matching algorithms using common identifiers (PINs) as well as non-unique identifiers (name, sex, date of birth, geographic codes). De-duplication and Conflict Resolution Rules: Establishing decision-tree logic and priority rules (weighting recency, source reliability, and cross-register agreement) when handling contradictory entries across sources. Signs of Life (SOL) Methodology: Implementing SOL activity markers (e.g., active health visits, school enrolment, tax/pension contributions, utility activity) to filter out latent over-coverage (unreported emigrations/deaths) from the baseline population. Module 4: Establishing the Statistical Population Register (SPR) and Base Registers CAPMAS will be guided in designing the conceptual and database architecture of an internal, secondary Statistical Population Register that serves as the backbone for census operations. Architectural Blueprint: Designing the SPR architecture within CAPMAS, linking individual statistical IDs to base registers: oStatistical Population Register (SPR): Serving as the national population spine. oBuilding/Dwelling Register & Master Address File: Linking individual usual residence to physical coordinates (𝑥,𝑦) and structural units. oStatistical Business Register (SBR): Linking working individuals to enterprise locations for workplace/industry statistics. Pre-filling Field Enumeration: Formulate pre-filling rules for the 2028 combined census field instruments. Train CAPMAS on how register-based data can be securely pre-filled onto tablets for doorstep verification and updating by field enumerators, managing the risk of enumerator bias. Triangulation and Benchmarking: Develop methods to triangulate administrative register counts, mobile phone estimates, and full field enumeration results to evaluate coverage and adjust statistical weights. Module 5: Microdata Protection, Anonymization & Confidentiality This module operates strict data protection protocols to prevent the disclosure of individual and institutional identities. Data Masking and Hashing: Implementing secure, automated one-way hashing algorithms to replace administrative National IDs with pseudonymous internal Statistical IDs. Statistical Disclosure Control (SDC): Applying SDC tools for small-area tabulations to preserve individual confidentiality. Five Safes Framework: Designing operational protocols around Safe Data, Safe Projects, Safe People, Safe Settings, and Safe Outputs.
